# Data {#sec-data}

Parent-reported vocabulary checklists record a subset of the words a child knows, speaks or signs.

## Measures

The sources use MacArthur-Bates CDI Words and Gestures and Words and Sentences forms, the Oxford CDI, DSE checklists and related adaptations. Their item lists and response options differ. The [data source notes](../../data/readme.md) record the known measurement details.

The common 810-item reference is a modelling scale, not evidence that the forms contain the same words. Counts are not multiplied by a checklist-length ratio. Each form's own ceiling is retained in the prepared data. @sec-reference-inventory describes the assumptions and checks on this choice.

### Signing measures

Signing columns differ in what they count. `uk_01` records sign-only words and cannot identify total signing from its aggregate fields, so the primary signing models mask that field while retaining comprehension and speech. A named sensitivity reintroduces it. The source confirmed that `uk_06` uses standard DSE checklists, whose signing column includes imitated and spontaneous signs. Its field is therefore retained as total signing. The [source records](../../data/readme.md) document these decisions and the overlap categories available in other studies.

## Studies

We pool data from a variety of sources, including data collected by charities and research groups across multiple countries.

### A study of vocabulary, signing and grammatical complexity in 218 children with Down syndrome (uk_01)

This study (Le Prevost, 2000, unpublished) collected data using the MacArthur Communicative Development Inventory (CDI), using both the Words and Gestures and Words and Sentences forms [@marchmanMacArthurBatesCommunicativeDevelopment2023; @fensonMacArthurCommunicativeDevelopment1993].  The data were collected through several research projects at The Sarah Duffen Centre, a joint initiative of the University of Portsmouth and Down Syndrome Education International (then the Portsmouth Down's Syndrome Trust). Parents were provided with the form appropriate for their child's age. In many instances, adapted versions were used. In addition to the standard "understands" and "understands and says" options, the adapted Words and Gestures forms added an option to indicate if the child "signs" the word. The adapted Words and Sentences forms (which usually only include "says") added "understands" and "signs" as options. Each word takes one response, so a child's words understood are the words marked "understands", "understands and says" or "signs" together; no Words and Sentences form in the data supplied marks any word "understands", so this study's comprehension counts come from the Words and Gestures forms alone. Participants were 218 children with Down syndrome between 1 and 9 years of age, including 102 girls and 116 boys. Words and Sentences was completed by 154 participants and Words and Gestures was completed by 64 participants. The families participating lived in the five closest counties to Portsmouth: Hampshire, West Sussex, Surrey, Dorset and Wiltshire.

### The development of vocabulary in Spanish children with Down syndrome: comprehension, production, and gestures (es_01)

This data was collected as part of a study on the development of vocabulary in Spanish children with Down syndrome [@galeoteDevelopmentVocabularySpanish2011]. The participants included 186 children with Down syndrome aged 11 to 71 months. All children had a monolingual Spanish background. The participating families were contacted through early intervention units and Down syndrome parent associations from different cities in Spain (mainly in the South). The study used an adapted CDI form consisting of 651 words organised into 21 categories, with options to record "understands" and "understands and says". In addition, the form included a third column to assess the comprehension and production of gestures representing specific lexical items. Symbolic gestures were defined as those gestures that, when properly taught or spontaneously learnt, substitute specific lexical items (e.g., closing the hand with tight fingers and moving it towards the mouth to simulate "to eat"). The gesture column is therefore a per-word record of manual expression, taught signs and spontaneously learnt gestures alike, which the source does not separate; the authors use *signed* and *gestured* interchangeably, and parents were asked to mark only words "produced or signed referentially and spontaneously". The study's own typically developing comparison group, with no sign instruction reported, averaged 23.6 gestured words, so spontaneous symbolic gesture is captured. No other signing source in the pool records what its parents were told a sign is, so the column is read as this study's signed count on the same footing as the others, with one measurement caveat: after a validity check the authors eliminated eleven of the form's 21 word categories from the gesture data, and whether the totals supplied to us carry that elimination is being confirmed with the author.

### See and Learn, Down Syndrome Ireland (ie_01)

This data was collected by Down Syndrome Ireland as part of a project from 2019 to 2020.

### Vocabulary development in Italian children with Down syndrome (it_01)

This data was collected as part of two studies investigating longitudinal trends in vocabulary development and cross-sectional data for Italian children with Down syndrome [@zampiniVocabularyDevelopmentChildren2013].

In the first study, 18 children with Down syndrome were studied longitudinally, including 10 children who were 2 years old and were followed for a 2-year period until they reached the age of 4 years. Moreover, eight other 3-year-old children were followed for a 1-year period until they reached the age of 4 years. For the second study, 27 children were selected from the sample of 60 toddlers attending our monitoring program on language development. The inclusion criteria for these children were a developmental age of approximately 18 (M = 18.22, range: 16–20), 24 (M = 24.11, range: 23–25), and 30 (M = 29.22, range: 28–30) months. Nine children were included in each group.

The study descriptions above are examples, not a complete source catalogue. The [data guide](../../data/readme.md) links every source record, including preparation rules and measurement limits. The summary tables below describe the prepared pool. Individual model reports record the rows used after model-specific restrictions.

## Repeated measures {#sec-repeated-measures}

Many children are measured more than once, and the within-child trajectories motivate the models' subject-level random effects. In the figures below each line joins one child's visits on one checklist form, drawn against the pooled median, mean and interquartile range for that age window (computed over all observations, single-visit children included). Lines are linked **within form only**: a child measured on two forms at one visit, or moved between forms, records counts on different item inventories, and joining those would draw measurement-scale changes as development. The Down syndrome figures cover an 8–72 month display window. Differences between the lines can reflect child differences, assessment variation and study effects. A change between visits is not, by itself, an estimate of a child's underlying learning rate.

![Words understood by age, repeated measures in the pooled Down syndrome data, coloured by study, against the pooled median (solid), mean (dashed) and interquartile band.](figures/descriptives/repeat_measures_age_understood_ds){#fig-rm-understood-ds .lightbox}

![Words spoken by age, repeated measures in the pooled Down syndrome data, coloured by study, against the pooled median (solid), mean (dashed) and interquartile band.](figures/descriptives/repeat_measures_age_spoken_ds){#fig-rm-spoken-ds .lightbox}

The same view of the typically-developing Wordbank reference pool, over its 8–30 month admission window (3-month bins; comprehension is measured only on the bivariate forms, so the understood panel ends where those forms do):

![Words understood by age, repeated measures in the typically-developing reference pool, coloured by dataset.](figures/descriptives/repeat_measures_age_understood_td){#fig-rm-understood-td .lightbox}
